subject: Follow-up: data placement, logs, and failover for NexaHealth POC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: data placement, logs, and failover for NexaHealth POC

Hi Daniel —

Great to meet you and the NexaHealth team on today's call. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the POC and the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what we heard:
- You need POC-ready inference for a clinical triage assistant that will process patient-entered text (PII present).
- Residency requirement: primary data residency in US (East) with a requirement to demonstrate cross-region failover to US (West) or EU for regulatory testing.
- Audit/logging: you need request/response logging for troubleshooting, but would like controls to mask or avoid storing direct identifiers where possible.
- Retention: default retention must be configurable per-environment and support 30/90/365-day retention windows; longer-term archival needs authorization.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm below):
1) Is PII stored in your prompts/responses a hard no for long-term logs, or would short-term (30d) encrypted logs be acceptable for the POC?
2) For failover testing, do you require continuous replication of KV caches state across regions, or is a cold/warm failover acceptable where the model spins up in the target region and absorbs traffic?
3) Who on your team will own the compliance checklist? (I note an earlier mention of Security; including them on the next call will be helpful.)

What Redwood can offer for the POC (high-level):
- Hosted API with region-targeted placement (US-East primary). We can route traffic to US-West as warm standby; cold-start times are measurable and we can provide a failover playbook.
- Dedicated or Private deployments (if you need complete data plane isolation). These let you keep all data and logs within your VPC.
- Logging controls: configurable policy for token-level retention, redact-on-ingest hooks, and an opt-in for full request logging for debugging.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots at customer-defined intervals; we can scope an RPO/RTO target for the POC.

Attachments: I'm including a short SOC 2 summary and a rough placement/failover diagram for reference.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive with Monica (solutions engineer) and Marcus (product infra) to walk through failover sequence and logging mechanics. 60 minutes.
- You to share your security questionnaire (we can fill the items relevant to POC).

Availability: Monica and Marcus are available Mon/Tue mornings next week PST. Does 2028-04-09 10:00 PST work for a 60-minute session?

Thanks — I'll put a calendar hold tentatively for that time until I hear back.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (pdf), placement-failover-diagram.png (image)
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@nexahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@nexahealth.com
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data placement, logs, and failover for NexaHealth POC

Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers and one doc attached (security Qs).

Answers:
1) For the POC we can accept short-term (30d) encrypted logs for debugging, but anything retained beyond that requires explicit approval from our compliance team.
2) Warm failover is acceptable for the POC. Long-term we may evaluate active-active, but that's not a blocker for initial testing.
3) Security will own the questionnaire (copied). Procurement will handle the order after we validate technical fit.

One additional ask: does Redwood provide any built-in PII redaction or field-level masking before logs are persisted? If not, what's the recommended pattern?

I've attached our security questionnaire (nexa_security_qs_filled.xlsx) — if you could pre-populate the POC-relevant sections that would be great.

Daniel
Director, Cloud Architecture
NexaHealth

Attachment: nexa_security_qs_filled.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 14:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data placement, logs, and failover for NexaHealth POC

Thanks Daniel — glad to have the questionnaire. We've filled the POC sections and attached the completed sheet (see attached). Below are direct answers to your PII/logging questions and some operational notes that will help scope the technical session.

PII redaction / masking options (Redwood capabilities):
- Redact-on-ingest hooks: customers can supply a pre-ingest Lambda-style hook that inspects and rewrites request payloads. Useful for deterministic removal of identifiers before logging.
- Field-level redaction in the logging pipeline: you can configure patterns (regex/email, ssn, phone) to be scrubbed before persistence. This is supported for Hosted and Dedicated plans; for Private we can apply customer-managed tooling in the VPC.
- Token filtering and metadata-only logs: by default we store request metadata (request id, timestamp, model id, token counts). Full request/response bodies are opt-in for debugging and can be time-limited (e.g., 30-day retention).

Data residency and failover behavior:
- Placement: For Hosted, you can pin production traffic to US-East. We maintain control-plane metadata in our control region, but customer data can be restricted to target regions per your policy.
- Failover: For the POC we recommend warm standby in US-West. Behavior is: primary serves traffic; when health checks fail, traffic is routed to standby region; KV cache is not continuously replicated by default (due to performance/cost tradeoffs), so warm standby will have empty KV state and will rebuild on traffic. We can run a short replication experiment if you need KV warm-sync for session continuity.
- Backups: encrypted, customer-key (KMS) compatible snapshots; retention windows configurable, and we can export snapshots to your cloud account for long-term archiving.

Operational controls and recommended defaults for your POC:
- Logging: enable metadata-only logging by default; enable full logging for a specific sandbox environment with 30-day retention for triage.
- Retention: set 30-day retention for logs in POC; archival to customer's bucket only after security approval.
- Monitoring: we'll provide a per-route latency/cost dashboard and a tracing hook for 1% sampled traces to preserve performance data without keeping full payloads.

Attachments included: updated nexa_security_qs_filled.xlsx (POC answers) and a short diagram that calls out failover sequence.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive on 2028-04-09 at 10:00 PST (Monica + Marcus). We'll review: redaction hooks, failover runbook, preliminary RPO/RTO numbers, and fill out any remaining security checklist items.
- Post-call deliverable: short POC runbook (1–2 pages) and an order-of-magnitude SOW for procurement.

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite and attach the pre-populated questionnaire.

Best,
Evelyn
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nexa_security_qs_filled.xlsx (updated), placement-failover-diagram.png (updated)

Evelyn / team — thanks, that level of detail is perfect. 10:00 PST on 2028-04-09 works for our side; we've accepted the invite.

Two quick asks ahead of the call:
1) Can you circulate the 1–2 page POC runbook (bullet list with success criteria and RPO/RTO targets) right after the call? Procurement wants that doc for internal approval.
2) If possible, include a short example config snippet showing the redact-on-ingest hook (or pseudo-code) so our engineers can review before the session.

I'll have security and one person from procurement join the call. Post-call we can move to an internal review and (if all good) get the PO out within two weeks.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
Daniel
Director, Cloud Architecture
NexaHealth
